newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore diesel at five-year high, fuel oil down.
newsitem.headline: Singapore diesel at five-year high, fuel oil down.

text.p: Singapore gas oil traded on Thursday at a five-year high of $30.00 per barrel on expectations of renewed buying interest from China and Indonesia, traders said.
Traders said Shell Singapore sold 150,000 barrels loading Oct 27-31 to a Japanese trading house and another buyer was seen for a November cargo at $29.85 per barrel.

The sale comes on talk of the emergence of limited buying from China. Traders said China bought at least three cargoes recently for arrival in end October or early November at between $227-$230 per tonne cost-and-freight.
They also said majors in Hong Kong were importing increased volumes for barge-lot sales on ex-terminal basis to traders who are exporting to China.
The market also firmed on talk of new buying from Indonesia which is not operating its 200,000-bpd Cilacap crude unit at full capacity, traders said.

Ample jet fuel offers were seen for late October cargoes at $30.50 but buyers were targeting $29.75. Traders said stocks in the Gulf were high and cargoes for loading in October are still available at premiums of between flat to 10 cents above Middle East quotes.
Naphtha edged down slightly in line with weaker overnight crude values. November swaps was quoted at $22.20/22.40, down from Wednesday's close of $22.60/22.70.
Gasoline firmed and was bid for 92-octane at $25.45, up 20 cents from Wednesday.
High sulphur fuel oil prices fell in line with lower crude and an absence of physical buying interest. Swaps fell with October traded at $120.50, from Wednesday's $122.00.
Traders said one major was offered a physical cargo down to $122.00 per tonne, down from Wednesday's five-year high trade of $124.00. -- Singapore newsroom (65-870-3093)
